hypotheses_not_runtime_evidence: An actor with real UID retained as issuer and effective UID ROOT can be credential-signalable; the present full startup tree has not proved that property.
The actual sudo execution route and PGID/SID coverage may differ from assumptions. No pre-drop ROOT chain was executed in the metadata run.

A dedicated NONROOT supervisor with effective CAP_KILL in the target user namespace could directly signal ROOT, but no authenticated grant/bootstrap or capability confinement proof is presently available.
An upstream conditional EPERM path is not a historical ROOT EPERM observation. The kernel is not declared unsupported.

claims.claim: Sender real/effective UID matching target real/saved UID, or CAP_KILL in target user namespace, supplies credential permission; other security hooks may still deny.
Process-group signalling can return success when at least one member accepts delivery. killpg SENT alone does not prove delivery to all ROOT members.

File capabilities or set-id changes clear ambient capabilities at exec. Normal Python exec does not retain prior effective CAP_KILL merely because its caller had it; ambient/file-capability transfer needs an explicit design.
Command credentials are applied using setresuid(real,effective,effective).
Depending on policy/flags, sudo may exec the command directly instead of maintaining a forwarding process.
The non-pty monitoring route forwards handled signals to its command PID. This route is not universal and cannot forward SIGKILL through a userspace handler.
PERM_ROOT can set real/effective/saved UID all to ROOT during sudoers processing, so command-level UID retention alone does not establish continuous startup custody.
stay_setuid supplies invoking-user real UID with target effective UID for command execution.
stay_setuid is documented as off by default; actual runner policy is unverified.

permanent_guard_recommendations: Keep privileged_signal_custody exactly NO_VERIFICADO/proved=false/privileged_launch_authorized=false until genuine full-tree evidence exists.
Readiness metadata, module availability and workflow success must not authorize ROOT or qualify capacity.
Preserve physical NOT_CALLED assertions for namespace creation, image allocation and root-worker launch on every unknown custody path.
Unknown FIN or live loop/mount custody must veto payload reads and outer cleanup; preserve controls without manufacturing inner FIN.
Test negative partial killpg delivery, UID-reset startup, escaped process group, missing capability grant and backend capability inheritance before any promotion.

required_authority_and_proofs.bootstrap: A previously authenticated privileged entry mechanism whose complete startup is signalable by the issuer, or a previously authenticated dedicated CAP_KILL supervisor. Neither is established by current evidence.
required_authority_and_proofs.capability_confinement: No API/Git credentials to ROOT; no ambient/effective/permitted/inheritable CAP_KILL at backend entry; no shared interpreter/filecap changes.
required_authority_and_proofs.fin: Actual primary/adopted wait4 reaps, ECHILD, owned group absent and subreaper restoration within unchanged TERM2/FIN5. A self-timeout exit or wrapper boolean cannot credit signal delivery.
required_authority_and_proofs.financial_effects: None: no financial tick, workload reduction, promotion, deployment or runtime-validation claim.
finite_stop_cases: ROOT ignores TERM and receives genuine KILL
required_authority_and_proofs.whole_tree: Bind every actor and child by PID/birth, real/effective/saved UID, user namespace, PGID/SID and owned ancestry; demonstrate coverage of Original killpg without relying on partial-success SENT.
